text:
ConocoPhillips fell almost imperceptibly today after a five-day run-up of 5.3%, closing essentially flat at $134.10. The stock has been rising sharply since October 2nd on the back of crude oil prices climbing — the global oil price jumped to $125.44 per barrel this week — fueled by supply disruptions from tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, refinery damage from regional conflicts, and Hurricane Isaias hitting Gulf of Mexico production. Today's tiny decline suggests a pause in that momentum rather than a reversal of the underlying bullish picture.

The broader setup remains supportive for oil majors: there's a wide gap between U.S. oil prices ($96.24) and world prices ($125.44), reflecting tight supply and refining constraints that typically benefit producers like ConocoPhillips. Even the Trump-Putin diesel deal announced this week, which might eventually ease fuel scarcity, has not yet translated into lower crude prices or dampened the geopolitical risk premium that's been lifting energy stocks.
